name: Paul McCartney
milestone_by_age_26: Co-wrote and released the Beatles' debut single 'Love Me Do' in October 1962 at age 20, launching a career that produced multiple chart-topping albums and singles and global Beatlemania by age 26.
early_history_summary: McCartney met John Lennon at 15 in 1957 and joined his skiffle group the Quarrymen. The Beatles formed in 1960, played extended residencies in Hamburg, and signed to EMI/Parlophone in 1962, releasing their first single that October.
family_context_summary: McCartney grew up in a working-class Liverpool family; his mother was a nurse/midwife and the primary wage earner, while his father was a cotton merchant salesman and former jazz musician. The family lived in council housing in Speke.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Jim McCartney was a trumpet player and pianist who led Jim Mac's Jazz Band in the 1920s, kept an upright piano in the front room, and encouraged Paul to be musical from a young age, giving him a trumpet for his 14th birthday.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lennon-McCartney partnership, father musician, grammar school, Liverpool scene, mother's death, Hamburg gigs
evidence_summary: McCartney's father was a jazz musician who encouraged music at home, providing early domain exposure and a piano in the house. The defining early advantage was the Lennon-McCartney songwriting partnership formed at 15, which created an exceptionally complementary creative team. Liverpool's emerging beat music scene and the Hamburg gig circuit provided direct performance experience from age 17. His mother's death at 14 created adversity that bonded him with Lennon, who had also lost his mother. He passed the 11-plus exam and attended the Liverpool Institute grammar school.

name: George R. R. Martin
milestone_by_age_26: Sold his first professional science fiction story 'The Hero' to Galaxy magazine in 1970 at age 21, and by age 26 had multiple published stories including the Hugo and Nebula-nominated 'With Morning Comes Mistfall' (1973).
early_history_summary: Martin began writing and selling monster stories to neighborhood children as a child, became active in comics fandom as a teenager, won an Alley Award for fan fiction at 17, and graduated summa cum laude from Northwestern in journalism in 1970. He began selling professional SF stories the same year.
family_context_summary: Martin grew up in a working-class family in Bayonne, New Jersey; his father was a longshoreman and his mother's family had once been wealthy but lost everything in the Great Depression. The family lived in a federal housing project near the Bayonne docks.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence that Martin's parents had relevant domain expertise in writing, literature, or publishing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Early writing practice, SF fandom, Northwestern journalism, constrained childhood drove imagination
evidence_summary: Martin grew up in a working-class family in a federal housing project with no family connections to writing or publishing. His early advantage was self-created: voracious reading, writing monster stories as a child, active participation in SF and comics fandom communities including fanzines and the first Comic-Con, and formal journalism training at Northwestern (summa cum laude). The constrained geography of his childhood fueled his imagination and drive to create fictional worlds.

name: Giacomo Agostini
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 500cc World Championship in 1966 at age 23, followed by 500cc titles in 1967 and 1968, and the 350cc title in 1968, amassing four world championships by age 26.
early_history_summary: Agostini began racing in 1963 and won the Italian national 350cc title in 1964. His performance caught the attention of Count Domenico Agusta, who signed him to the MV Agusta factory team for 1965. He won his first Grand Prix in 1965 and became 500cc World Champion in 1966.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MV Agusta factory team, Italian racing culture, exceptional riding talent, factory equipment, Count Agusta mentorship
evidence_summary: Agostini's early career was defined by his exceptional riding talent, which caught the attention of Count Domenico Agusta, who signed him to the elite MV Agusta factory team. Italy's position as a center of motorcycle racing provided natural domain proximity. The MV Agusta team provided elite-level equipment, mechanics, and infrastructure. No family background information was documented in reviewed sources.

name: Mario Botta
milestone_by_age_26: Designed his first building, a two-family house at Morbio Superiore, at age 16, and by age 26 had apprenticed with Carloni and Camenisch, studied at the Art College in Milan and Iuav in Venice, and worked with renowned architects Le Corbusier, Louis Kahn, and Carlo Scarpa.
early_history_summary: Botta dropped out of secondary school at 15 to apprentice with an architectural firm in Lugano, designed his first building at 16, then studied at the Art College in Milan and Iuav in Venice, where he worked with Le Corbusier, Louis Kahn, and Carlo Scarpa before graduating in 1969.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Early apprenticeship, Le Corbusier/Kahn/Scarpa mentorship, Iuav Venice, designed building at 16, architectural precocity
evidence_summary: Botta's defining early advantage was starting an architectural apprenticeship at 15 and designing a real building at 16, giving him direct domain exposure far earlier than typical. At Iuav Venice, he studied under Carlo Scarpa and had the extraordinary opportunity to work with Le Corbusier and Louis Kahn, three of the most influential architects of the 20th century. This combination of early practical experience and elite mentorship accelerated his development significantly. No family background information was documented.

name: Demis Roussos
milestone_by_age_26: Released solo single 'We Shall Dance' in 1971 at age 25, which was a top ten hit in the Netherlands and Belgium, while also achieving international success with progressive rock band Aphrodite's Child.
early_history_summary: Roussos studied music and sang in a Byzantine choir in Alexandria as a child, then moved to Greece after the Suez Crisis in 1956. He joined his first band at 17, met Vangelis, and formed Aphrodite's Child, which achieved international success before he launched a solo career in 1971.
family_context_summary: Roussos was born into a Greek family in Alexandria, Egypt. His father was a classical guitarist and engineer, and his mother participated in amateur theater. The family lost their possessions during the Suez Crisis in 1956 and moved to Greece.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a classical guitarist and engineer, and his mother was an amateur singer who performed in a Greek theatrical group in Alexandria, providing early musical and artistic exposure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Father guitarist, mother singer, Byzantine choir, Vangelis collaboration, Suez Crisis displacement
evidence_summary: Roussos grew up in a musical household in Alexandria: his father was a classical guitarist and his mother an amateur singer. He received early vocal training through the Greek Church Byzantine choir. The Suez Crisis forced the family to relocate to Greece, creating adversity that catalyzed his musical career. At 17, he met Vangelis, forming a key collaborative partnership in Aphrodite's Child that led to international success and his solo breakthrough by 25.

name: Arvydas Sabonis
milestone_by_age_26: Won three consecutive Soviet Premier League championships with Žalgiris (1985-1987) and the 1986 FIBA Club World Cup, while also being a key member of the Soviet national team from 1982, all by age 26.
early_history_summary: Sabonis began playing basketball at 13 in Kaunas and by 15 was on the Soviet national junior team. He made his professional debut with Žalgiris in 1981 at age 16 and quickly became one of the dominant players in Soviet basketball, leading to three consecutive league titles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet national team, Žalgiris, exceptional height, early specialization, Lithuanian basketball culture
evidence_summary: Sabonis's early career was defined by his exceptional physical attributes (7'3" height) and early entry into the Soviet elite sports pipeline. He began playing at 13, joined the national junior team at 15, and debuted professionally at 16 with Žalgiris. The Soviet system provided elite coaching, facilities, and competitive infrastructure. Lithuania's strong basketball culture provided domain proximity. No family background was documented in reviewed sources.

name: Miguel Induráin
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional in September 1984 at age 20, won his first professional race at the Tour de l'Avenir, became the youngest rider to lead the Vuelta a España in 1985, and won a stage of the Tour de France in 1989, all by age 26.
early_history_summary: Induráin received his first bicycle at 10, started racing at 14 in 1978, and won the Spanish amateur national road championship at 18 as the youngest ever winner. He turned professional in 1984 with the Reynolds team and immediately won a stage at the Tour de l'Avenir.
family_context_summary: Induráin grew up in the village of Villava near Pamplona, Spain. He has three sisters and a brother who also became a professional cyclist. His first bicycle was a secondhand Olmo given for his 10th birthday; when it was stolen, he worked in the fields with his father to pay for a replacement.
parent_family_domain_summary: His brother Prudencio also became a professional cyclist, suggesting a family environment supportive of cycling, but no evidence of parental domain expertise was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Exceptional physiology, early racing, youngest amateur champion, Spanish cycling culture, brother cyclist
evidence_summary: Induráin's early career was built on exceptional physical attributes that manifested early: he was the youngest ever winner of the Spanish amateur national road championship at 18. He grew up in a modest farming family in Navarra and had to work in the fields to replace a stolen bicycle. His brother also became a professional cyclist, suggesting a supportive family environment. The local cycling culture and CC Villavés club provided early competitive infrastructure, leading to professional status at 20 with the Reynolds team.

name: Lars von Trier
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, won two Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools for 'Nocturne' and 'Last Detail,' and had his graduation film 'Images of Liberation' released as a theatrical feature.
early_history_summary: Von Trier studied film theory at the University of Copenhagen and film direction at the National Film School of Denmark. He made short films from a young age, won awards at the Munich film festival for his student work, and had his graduation film released theatrically, launching his professional career.
family_context_summary: Von Trier grew up in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark. His parents were Inger Høst and Ulf Trier; he later learned his biological father was Fritz Michael Hartmann, a former resistance fighter and his mother's boss at the Ministry of Social Affairs. He was brought up in an atheist household with communist and social democratic political influences.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence that von Trier's parents had expertise in film or the arts. His biological father came from a family of classical composers (grandson of Emil Hartmann), but this connection was unknown to von Trier during his formative years.
primary_early_advantage_tags: National Film School of Denmark, Munich festival awards, early filmmaking, European art cinema, unconventional family
evidence_summary: Von Trier's early career was shaped by formal film education at the National Film School of Denmark, one of Europe's elite institutions. He made films from childhood and won Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools at 25, with his graduation film receiving theatrical release. His family background was unconventional—he later discovered his biological father was not the man who raised him—but this was unknown during his formative years and did not provide domain advantage.

name: Luis Enrique
milestone_by_age_26: Made his La Liga debut with Sporting Gijón in September 1989 at age 19, joined Real Madrid in 1991 at age 21, and earned his first cap for Spain in April 1991, establishing himself as a top-flight professional and international by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Luis Enrique grew up in Gijón, Asturias, and joined local club Sporting de Gijón's youth system at age 11. He progressed through the youth and B teams before breaking into the first team in 1989, then earned a transfer to Real Madrid in 1991.
family_context_summary: Luis Enrique was born in Gijón, Asturias, Spain. No specific family background information was documented in reviewed sources.

evidence_summary: Luis Enrique's early career was built on the Spanish football development pipeline: he joined Sporting Gijón's youth system at 11 in his hometown of Gijón, progressed through the ranks, and debuted in La Liga at 19. name: Miuccia Prada
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (May 1974), Prada had a political science degree and was performing as a mime artist and involved in leftist politics. She did not enter the family fashion business until the mid-1970s (around age 27-28), took over Prada in 1978 at age 30, and had her first successful design in 1985 at age 37. No material fashion/design milestone by age 26 found.
family_context_summary: Prada was born Maria Bianchi in Milan in 1948 into an affluent bourgeois Catholic family. She was the youngest granddaughter of Mario Prada, who founded the Prada luxury goods company in 1913. She was adopted by an aunt and took the name Miuccia Prada in the 1980s.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her grandfather Mario Prada founded the Prada luxury leather goods company in 1913, providing a family business in luxury fashion. However, Prada did not enter this business until her late 20s, and her parents' direct involvement is not clearly documented.
